about.text: Cheese made by heating the buttermilk left from churning soured milk until its proteins curdle, then draining the curd. The cheese of the Himalaya, Ethiopia and Anatolia: soft chhurpi, datshi, ayib and çökelek.

links.name: Food Science & Nutrition (2022), on Bhutanese datshi

picture.author: Nair A, Choden D, Pradhan M.

sources.text: The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

how.text: The churned, already soured buttermilk is heated, so the heat-denatured proteins clump with the remaining acid; the solid is separated from the liquid and drained. No rennet. Himalayan kinds are boiled; ayib is warmed only to about 40-50 °C.

steps.note: Boiled until the protein curdles (Himalaya), while ayib is warmed only to about 40–50 °C.
Soft chhurpi is often left to ferment a little for tang.
